item.text: I’m isolating the UI responsibilities now. First I’ll map the current `SimulatorView` rendering flow and identify the clean seams for a rendering strategy and color policy, then I’ll move the paint logic behind those abstractions without changing what the window shows.

I’ve confirmed the current UI still mixes three concerns: widget assembly, status text generation, and paint-time cell styling. I’m reading the tail of the view class before editing so I can split those concerns cleanly and keep the rendering pipeline behavior identical.

I’m checking how widely the current view API is used before I reshape it. If `setInfoText` or color registration is only internal, I can simplify the facade further and keep the public surface stable where the simulator actually depends on it.

I’ve got the boundaries now, and I’m making the view a thin façade: labels, canvas, and delegation only. The new strategy will own the color map, the `FieldStats`, and the actual per-cell rendering rules, which is the part that currently makes `SimulatorView` hard to extend.

I’m replacing `SimulatorView` wholesale rather than patching it piecemeal. That gives a clean separation: the frame owns components, while the strategy handles all coloring, counting, and per-cell rendering decisions.

I’ve finished the UI split and I’m compiling now. If anything breaks, it’ll likely be from the new canvas interface or from the simulator still doing redundant color setup that I can strip once the new default strategy is confirmed.
I’m trimming one last piece of simulator-side UI boilerplate: the hardcoded color registration. The strategy now owns the defaults, so `Simulator` shouldn’t need to know about palette setup at all.
The build is clean. I’m doing a small polish pass now to remove the leftover UI imports and make the custom paint component follow Swing conventions a bit more closely.
